recipe: Ras el hanout chicken thighs over sultana & almond couscous
servesNote: 2 portions — Karl 3 : Maria 2. Of ~5 thighs, Karl 3 and Maria 2; the couscous splits the same way. Maria's next-day lunch comes out of this and is very good.
adaptations: ⚠️ THE PASTE SACHETS ARE NOT IN THE HOUSE. The library card asks for one sachet each of tomato paste and roasted garlic paste. Both were recorded OUT on 3 Sep — they are the two that were caught at the pan. Tuesday's shop bought jars instead: use 2 tbsp of the tomato double concentrate (200 g tube) and 1 tbsp of the Ready Set Cook! chopped garlic (200 g jar). Same job, and the jars mean this stops being a one-outing dish.

⭐ The chopped garlic is raw, where the sachet was roasted and sweeter. It goes into the paste and then under the skin, so it gets 45 minutes at 220°C and comes out mellow. Do not be tempted to add extra to compensate up front.

⚠️ RAS EL HANOUT IS SACHETS ONLY, no jar behind it, and the house held two. Use one. If the box is empty, 1 tsp cumin + ½ tsp coriander + ½ tsp cinnamon + ½ tsp paprika + a grind of pepper gets close enough to cook from — this dish is carried by the rendered fat and the lemon more than by the blend.

prep: ⭐ THIGHS OUT AND SALTED THE MOMENT YOU WALK IN — everything else fits inside the ten minutes this needs. Out of the pack, pat every surface dry INCLUDING UNDER THE LOOSE FLAP OF SKIN, then scatter 1 tsp Maldon over the skin, crushing it between your fingers. Leave uncovered on a plate. The salt draws moisture to the surface and it evaporates; skin cannot begin to brown until its surface is dry. Ten minutes of this is worth more than any amount of oil later.
Oven to 220°C / 200°C fan, with the large roasting tin inside as it heats. The vegetables should hit hot metal, not cold.
Toss the onion wedges and carrots with 1 tbsp oil, the cumin, paprika, cinnamon, ½ tsp salt and pepper. ⭐ Keep the onion wedges intact at the root so they go jammy rather than falling into strands.
Mix ½ tbsp oil with the ras el hanout, 2 tbsp tomato concentrate and 1 tbsp chopped garlic into a loose paste — a teaspoon of water only if it is too stiff to spread.
⭐ Rub the paste over the thighs, UNDER THE SKIN as well as on top, working a finger in at the edge to lift it. Spicing that sits on top is the commonest way this dish tastes flat.

steps.text: Pull out the hot tin, tip in the vegetables in a single layer, sit the thighs on top skin side up, spaced so none touch. Nothing piled up. A crowded tray steams. The veg below release plenty of moisture and that is the water the chicken needs — but the skin has to stay proud of it, in dry heat. Leave the tray uncovered.

Roast until the skin is deep bronze and taut, the fat has visibly rendered into the tray, and the onion tips are blackening at the edges. Pierced against the bone, the juice should run clear with no pink thread. ⚠️ Covering the tray fixes dryness and destroys the skin — a bone-in fatty cut will not dry out in this time.

Meanwhile, almonds into a small dry pan, shaking almost continuously until they smell nutty and the flat faces are pale-toast coloured. Tip straight onto a cold plate — left in the pan they carry on and turn bitter.

Couscous, sultanas, the chicken stock sachet and a pinch of salt into the heatproof bowl, plus the saffron crumbled between your fingers if using. Pour over 150 ml boiling water, stir ONCE, cover tightly with a plate, and leave it undisturbed. Do not stir again while it swells — that is what makes couscous pasty.
⭐ Rest the thighs on a board a full 8 minutes. Do not cover them tightly with foil, which softens the skin you just spent 45 minutes making.

Uncover the couscous — it should look swollen and dry. Drag a fork through in short strokes, lifting and separating rather than mixing, until every grain is loose. Add the toasted almonds and half the herbs.

⭐ Tip the vegetables and ALL the pan juices into the couscous, plus any juice pooled under the resting chicken, and fork through again. This is the step that makes the dish — the rendered chicken fat and spiced juices are the seasoning, and a version that serves couscous plain alongside has thrown them away.

Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon, taste, and add more salt and lemon until it tastes bright rather than heavy. The dish is sweet from the sultanas and the onions and needs the acid to stand up to them.

Serve with the thighs on top, the remaining herbs over, yoghurt on the side and lemon wedges. Maria's next-day lunch: strip the meat off the bones while warm and store it in the couscous — the meat stays moist and the couscous keeps absorbing. Yoghurt, lemon and a few almonds kept separate.
